claim_one_line: [CORRECTED 2026-08-26 -- THE CODEX SEAT IS MID-WORK AND RAN OUT OF USAGE; the characterization below is withdrawn and the facts are retained.] THE FACTS: on origin/codex/seat-r001, B1143's arc_verdict says banking the cloud's literal numbers 'would have been a FALSE POSITIVE ... a LOAD-BEARING ERROR, NOT A CONVENTION SLIP', and the branch has ZERO occurrences of any withdrawal; on origin/main the same arc, reframed by B1144, calls that correction WITHDRAWN as a CROSS-FRAME ARTIFACT, verified in golden_gate primary source. The codex seat's method was right and its signal was real -- the literal numbers do fail in B1139's frame -- and only the diagnosis changed. WHAT IS WITHDRAWN: my characterization of this as a live accusation, as graver than ordinary drift, and as something that 'should not sit'. AN INTERRUPTED BRANCH IS NOT ASSERTING ANYTHING. The seat ran out of usage mid-campaign; the missing withdrawal marks where the work stopped, not what the seat believes. The finding reduces to an ordinary handoff note for whoever resumes: B1144 reframed the catch, the detection stands, the class changed. AND THE ERROR CLASS IS MINE: I have insisted all campaign that an absence needs a search and a label needs a date. A mid-work branch has a date too, and I read a snapshot as a claim -- the same shape as reading a headline as a result. Compares one arc_verdict across two branches. Does not re-derive B-L, does not adjudicate the frame question -- main's B1144 did that against primary source and this seat accepts it. Gate 5 untouched.
